note: Morocco's (kept by Morocco and the Moroccan-administered Western Sahara): nationals of the countries listed (the EU, EFTA and the Gulf among them) enter without a visa for 90 days, 60 (the Dominican Republic), 30 (Hong Kong, the Maldives; Kazakhstan in 180); nationals of the Congo, Ecuador, Ghana and Guinea need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (AEVM) beforehand; nationals of Benin, Brunei, Cambodia, Guatemala, India, Israel, Jordan, Laos, Thailand and Vietnam may apply for an e-Visa; everyone else needs a visa from a mission (or an e-Visa if holding a Schengen, Australian, Canadian, Irish, Japanese, New Zealand, UAE, UK or US visa or residence: not modelled). Algeria's exemption is read as the list has it. Read from Wikipedia's copy.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Visa policy of Morocco
sources.said: Visitors to Morocco must obtain a visa unless they are citizens from one of the visa-exempt countries, or citizens who may obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (AEVM), or citizens eligible for an e-Visa . ... Citizens of the following countries and territories may enter Morocco without a visa for the following period: 90 days All European Union member states All European Free Trade Association member states All Gulf Cooperation Council member states Albania Algeria Andorra Argentina Australia Azerbaijan Brazil Burkina Faso Canada Cape Verde Chile China Colombia Gabon Indonesia Japan Macau Malaysia Mali Mexico Monaco New Zealand Niger Peru Philippines Russia San Marino Senegal Singapore South Korea Togo Tunisia Turkey United Kingdom United States 60 days Dominican Republic 30 days Hong Kong Maldives 30 days within any 180 days Kazakhstan ... Citizens of the following countries do not require a visa but must obtain an AEVM in advance to enter Morocco. Congo Ecuador Ghana Guinea ... Citizens of the following countries holding ordinary passports may apply for an e-Visa without further document requirement: Benin Brunei Darussalam Cambodia Guatemala India Israel Jordan Laos Thailand Vietnam
